key_idea: If n is even every block appears twice and any order of the distinct blocks works; if n is odd the blocks are exactly all cyclically adjacent pairs of half-blocks of p, so chain blocks by matching the second half of one to the first half of another.
sketch: n even: p is n/2 whole blocks, the second copy repeats them, so output each distinct block once (dedupe by first element) in any order. n odd (m even): cut p into n half-blocks x1..xn of length m/2; the first copy yields (x1x2),(x3x4),..., the middle block is (xn x1), the second copy yields (x2x3),...; together all n cyclic pairs. Index blocks by first element, start anywhere, repeatedly output the first half and jump to the block starting with the element at position m/2; any rotation of the cycle is a valid answer. O(nm) per test. Multiple answers are accepted, so the sample checker does not apply: validated with my own checker (regenerate blocks from the output and compare multisets) on the samples and 300 random cases.
